A.biggest_strength: True interactive freedom (continuous sliders for learning rate and start position, step/run/reset controls, live 4-decimal arithmetic table) paired with side-by-side small multiples comparing all three learning rates simultaneously.
A.biggest_weakness: At phone widths (390px), the top formula card and multi-column arithmetic table exceed container width and require horizontal scrolling.

B.biggest_strength: Structured pedagogical progression across five sequential concept scenes (Loss, Slope, One step, Repeat, Compare) with synchronized MathML equation displays and animated vector step indicators.
B.biggest_weakness: Premature rounding of intermediate values to 2 decimals causing the false claim that eta = 0.3 'lands on 3', combined with CSS uppercase transforming eta to 'H' in headings and an intrusive auto-advancing tour.
factual_errors: In Scene 3 and the data table, Page B claims and shows that with learning rate eta = 0.3, the updates 'land on 3' at step 7 with L'=0 and step=0. In reality, gradient descent with eta = 0.3 converges asymptotically (w_7 ≈ 2.9951, L'(w_7) ≈ -0.0098) and never lands exactly on 3 in finite steps; this zero-gradient termination is an artifact of cumulative 2-decimal truncation.

Applying CSS text-transform: uppercase to h2 and th elements converts the Greek letter eta (η) into Greek capital eta (Η), rendering headings as 'WHY THE FACTOR IS 1 − 2H', 'LEARNING RATE H', and 'FACTOR 1 − 2H', corrupting the mathematical notation into looking like the Latin letter H.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it offers an accurate, flexible, and student-friendly explainer where learners can inspect every number in live full precision and view all three learning rate regimes side-by-side. Page B severely limits interactivity to three fixed, precomputed runs, suffers from an intrusive auto-advancing carousel, corrupts its heading math symbols via CSS uppercase ('1 - 2H'), and misleads students by falsely showing that eta = 0.3 reaches the exact minimum and halts due to aggressive roundoff.
